equipment.name: IS Light Machine Gun Ammo - Full

fluff.overview: The Tenmaku is the command element of the Teppō combined arms system, a purpose-built seventy-five ton trailer designed to protect senior DCMS commanders during engagements while maintaining complete battlefield awareness. Developed concurrently with the Teppō by Pesht Motors and assembled at the same Unity facility, the Tenmaku translates the Ryuken regiments' informal command-and-control doctrine into a dedicated platform. By physically separating commanding officers from direct fire while keeping them connected to a real-time tactical picture, the Tenmaku addresses the DCMS's identified strategic vulnerability: the preventable loss of experienced staff through unnecessary proximity to the front line. The trailer is towed by the Teppō and is not designed for independent operation.
fluff.capabilities:
The Tenmaku carries ten tons of dedicated communications equipment, including a full satellite uplink and real-time integration with a holographic mapping system, giving an embarked commander visibility of every combat unit across a planetary engagement. Two C³ Master Computers extend this coordination network to an entire company of units. An infantry compartment provides space for attached command staff. The trailer sustains its systems through a self-contained 10-rated fusion reactor, operating independently of the Teppō's fuel cell.

Though the Tenmaku lacks independent mobility, it carries a defensive suite including pulse lasers, machine guns, and an anti-missile system capable of engaging infantry threats and lighter vehicles. The trailer shares the same heavy ferro-fibrous armor profile, anti-missile coverage, ECM protection, and CASE-protected ammunition bays found on the Teppō, presenting a uniform defensive character across the combined system. This consistency allows crews of both vehicles to train and maintain their equipment against the same threat parameters.
fluff.deployment: The Tenmaku operates exclusively as part of the Teppō combined arms system and is not designed for independent deployment. It is towed into position by the Teppō and relies on the artillery vehicle for all strategic and tactical movement. The first Tenmaku units were assigned alongside the Teppō to the Ryuken-san. Broader distribution was planned to follow the same allocation model as the Teppō itself, with each assigned system including both the Tenmaku and Bokkusu trailers as standard equipment.
fluff.history:
The Tenmaku was developed as the command element of the Teppō system under the same DCMS contract that produced the artillery vehicle, reflecting the same institutional lesson: the Ryuken regiments' post-Jihad survival record showed that effective command required physical protection, not merely communication efficiency. Development emphasis centered on maintaining comprehensive battlefield awareness from a hardened position, producing a platform where the commanding officer could monitor an entire planetary engagement in real time without direct exposure to enemy fire.

The Tenmaku's design drew directly from analysis of DCMS command casualties during the Jihad, which identified that senior officers leading from BattleMechs or light command vehicles suffered disproportionate losses relative to their contribution to unit effectiveness. By embedding command capability within a heavily protected trailer towed by one of the most durable vehicles on the battlefield, the system offered a practical alternative. Initial deployment to the Ryuken-san was deliberate, placing the Tenmaku with the brigade whose doctrinal history had directly inspired its creation. Broader DCMS adoption was planned contingent on the Teppō system's overall field evaluation.
